beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process repeatedly reads and updates it before decoding.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method separates the dense image field from the compact thought process that works on it. The encoder makes the feature field that carries spatial detail. Windowing breaks that field into token groups without changing the overall carrier. The DQ-CTM thought process runs shared ticks that read and update the carrier. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved image. The recurrence returns to the thought stage itself, so the same parameters are reused across ticks.

params.headline: ThinkSR routes dense features through shared recurrent thought

stages.label: DQ-CTM thought
stages.note: shared ticks read and update carrier

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features, then window partitioning forms tokens while preserving the dense feature field.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The equation defines the carrier before the thought process changes it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into a dense feature field. The window partition takes that field as input, so every token comes from the carrier rather than replacing it.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded first, then partitioned into windows
